articles.headline: Minkah Fitzpatrick healthy, ready to rejoin Jets. vs. Bears
articles.description: After suffering a groin injury in Week 1, Minkah Fitzpatrick said he will be back on the field with the Jets on Sunday against the Bears.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- After an abbreviated debut with the New York Jets, former All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick is poised to make his re-debut Sunday.

Fitzpatrick, who missed two games after injuring his groin on the sixth play of the season opener, practiced fully Thursday and proclaimed himself ready to play against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field.

He will rejoin a secondary mired in a historic interception drought. The Jets have gone 20 consecutive games without an interception -- 632 pass attempts, to be exact.

"It would be very nice, very sweet" to make the slump-busting interception in his return, Fitzpatrick said with a smile.

It was a frustrating September for Fitzpatrick, one of the Jets' key offseason additions. He was acquired from the Miami Dolphins in a trade and signed a three-year, $40 million contract.

Then came opening day against the Tennessee Titans.

"I started watching film on Tennessee probably in June, so I felt really, really locked in, really in tune with how the game was going to go and how it was going to flow," Fitzpatrick said. "And then six plays in, what happened happened.

"I tried my best to finish the game, but as a DB with the groin, it's kind of tough. So it was frustrating, but also at the same time, you still have to stay locked in. You can't be mad in those circumstances. I was still trying to help the teammates in the best way we can."

The Jets (1-2) have performed reasonably well without Fitzpatrick, who was replaced in the lineup by former starter Andre Cisco. Their defense is second in yards allowed (258 per game) and 12th in scoring (20.3 points), but it has only one takeaway -- a fumble recovery in Week 2 against the Green Bay Packers.

It's a familiar theme; the Jets had only four takeaways last season, a league mark for futility.

"I look at it like this: We just have to keep scratching, clawing, and fighting and they'll come our way," said coach Aaron Glenn, the defensive play-caller this season.

The Bears still haven't announced whether Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent will start in place of the injured Caleb Williams (hamstring). The Jets say they're preparing for both backups.

They know Ben Johnson's offense can be confusing, with its myriads of formations and pre-snap motion. Fitzpatrick, 29, a three-time first-team All-Pro, is a cerebral player who can be a steadying presence in the secondary.

"I think A.G. has gotten in a groove and has really figured out what he wants us to be as a defense in regards to schematics," Fitzpatrick said of Glenn. "So I think this week would just be the week that all things are clicking."

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Saints place RB Travis Etienne Jr. on IR
articles.description: Eric Moody evaluates which Saints RBs could see a greater share of the backfield after Etienne's move to IR.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 1: Saints place RB Etienne Jr. on IR

By Eric Moody

The New Orleans Saints placed RB Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, meaning he'll miss at least four games. With New Orleans' Week 8 bye, the earliest he can return is Week 9. That leaves Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller in line for more work in the backfield.

Kamara should get the first chance at leading the backfield. Etienne had taken on the largest share of the workload in Week 3 and finished with 13 carries despite leaving in the third quarter, while Kamara had nine and Miller had four.

Kamara hasn't been very efficient this season (2.8 YPC), but more touches could put him back in the RB2 conversation. He should see plenty of carries and remain involved in the passing game, giving him a solid floor as a flex option.

Miller should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Double-digit touches are possible with Etienne out, but I'd keep him on the bench until we get a better idea of how New Orleans plans to split the work.

Don't forget about CJ Donaldson, either. Coach Kellen Moore gave him the Saints' first touch inside the 10-yard line last week. If that continues, Donaldson could have a role near the goal line, even if Kamara and Miller handle most of the work.

Kamara is the one I'd feel comfortable starting right away. Miller belongs on rosters in 12-team leagues, while Donaldson is more of a deeper league player to monitor.

Dolphins move towards split backfield to replace Achane

By Marcel Louis-Jacques

Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II was one of the most popular adds in fantasy this week. The former Doak Walker Award winner offers rare size for the position and handled a 20-touch workload in place of De'Von Achane in Week 3.

We all know opportunity is a premium commodity in fantasy, but it's important to remember that Gordon was the Dolphins' only other active running back last week. Jaylen Wright, the former fourth-round pick, has seldom seen the field during his three-year career but ran for 107 yards and a touchdown on 24 carries filling in for Achane against the Jets last season.

Wright offers sub-4.40 speed and a versatile skill set. Speaking to Wright and Gordon this week, they sound ready to share the workload moving forward.

Dolphins Coach Jeff Hafley envisions a split backfield, so expect them to ride with the hot hand.

articles.headline: How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict
articles.description: As the reaction to Man City's guilty verdict continues to ripple across the sporting world, the club's internal messaging is very much one of confidence and carrying on. It may be easier said than done.
articles.body:
The strength of the judgement against Manchester City, following their legal case with the Premier League, has shocked the club, its employees and their players. Most of those inside the City Football Academy (CFA) accept that the verdict -- made public for the first time on Tuesday -- is a worst-case scenario.

There's been speculation and discussion on and off at the CFA for more than three years since the charges were announced in February 2023 about what might happen. It was always viewed internally as highly unlikely that every count of financial misconduct would be proved.

City insist they are innocent -- a message that's come from the top, namely chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano -- and many employees want to give the club the benefit of the doubt. They enjoy working for City and feel that they've been well looked after over the years.

In that respect, many people ESPN spoke for this story with are choosing to believe the conviction of Khaldoon and Soriano. At the very least, the majority of these staff members are prepared to wait until after the appeal is heard before passing judgement.

- Legal explainer: Man City have been charged. Now what?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City come back from seismic scandal

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict ruin Guardiola's legacy?

Many staff members are also fans and as such, they are personally invested as well as professionally. City are a big club and a major employer, but since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, they club's owners have done a good job of creating a family feel and a sense of shared purpose. More than 700 employees attended a UK all-staff meeting in the first week of this three-week international break, while players are away on duty with their national teams.

There is, however, a cloud hanging over the CFA, and the mood in general has been described to ESPN as nervous. Soriano, in his video message to staff on Tuesday, insisted it should be business as usual, but in the absence of any real information about what sanctions might follow, there's genuine worry about what the future could hold.

The same goes for the players. With many of City's senior squad away on international duty, some have had direct contact with the club, while others have not. One agent of a first-team player told ESPN that his client is "calm" about the situation and is happy with the public reassurances offered by senior executives. There is, though, an acceptance that things could change depending on the result of the appeal -- which has yet to be filed, but must be lodged by the close of business on Friday, Oct. 2 -- and any punishment handed down.

Player concerns

Speculation over considerable sporting sanctions is causing the most concern, sources tell ESPN. articles.headline: Joey Porter happy for fresh start with Cowboys, eyes Sunday debut
articles.description: Joey Porter Jr. says he hopes to make his debut for the Cowboys on Sunday, when they play the Texans.
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- When the week began, Joey Porter Jr. thought he would be playing Thursday night for the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Cleveland Browns. Now, he hopes to make his Dallas Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans.

"We're just trying to take things day by day," Porter said after his first practice in Dallas, "and if everything looks good, then we should be out there."

Porter was at the movie theater watching Brad Pitt's "Heart of the Beast" when he got word of the trade. The Cowboys gave up a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder to acquire Porter, marking the third deal the organizations have made since May 2025 (George Pickens, Broderick Jones).

Early Thursday morning, he was on a plane to join his new team, ending his run with the Steelers, who drafted him in the second round of the 2023 draft.

Porter was hoping for an extension with the Steelers, and the saga lasted throughout the offseason and into training camp while he dealt with a back injury. Porter said it was more his call not to play in against the Browns, but added that his back was "feeling better."

Porter is not listed on the Cowboys' injury report.

"It was a hard process; a lot of ups and downs," Porter said. "Definitely felt disrespected, definitely felt undervalued. But that's the old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm on to new beginnings, new chapters. And like I said, I'm a Cowboy. I'm in Dallas, so I'm happy about that."

Porter will have to wait for a possible extension from the Cowboys, too. Still, he said he would be open to finishing his career in Dallas.

"I'm down with it if they are. I want to finish my career here," Porter said. "So hopefully, I just perform like how I know how to perform and do what I do, and I'm going to let everything take care of the rest."

Through three games, the Cowboys are 25th in points allowed (27.3) and 30th in yards (387). The Cowboys are one of four teams without an interception.

With Cobie Durant (hamstring) expected to miss his second game and Shavon Revel Jr. not practicing much this week because of knee and ankle issues, the Cowboys almost need to have Porter immediately.

"This is more about you get a chance to get a young corner that's got elite cover skills that can come in and add to a group that's depleted right now with injuries is always good," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "But I think change of scenery is good."

It worked for Pickens, who had career highs in catches (93), yards (1,429) and touchdowns (nine) last season with the Cowboys.

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker used the term "boundary eraser" in his evaluation of Porter when he came out of Penn State. Though Porter has a reputation for his man-to-man skills, Parker said he saw him do enough work with the Steelers to know it won't be a difficult adjustment to the scheme. Parker said even if the Cowboys are in zone, they have some man principles.

articles.headline: NFL Week 4 uniforms: Browns wearing 'Alpha Dawg' look; Giants go 'Legacy'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 4, led by an alternate look from the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
As the calendar turns to October, NFL uniforms remain as fresh as ever with an alternate-heavy slate in Week 4. 

On "Thursday Night Football," the Cleveland Browns will wear their "Alpha Dawg" combination against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cleveland revealed the all-brown threads in July 2025 with a brand new alternate brown helmet. They debuted last season and marked the first time in franchise history that a brown helmet was worn. Orange-colored numbers run across the front and back of the jersey, as well as on the shoulder. There's also an orange stripe on the helmet.

In the throwback space, the New York Giants are donning their legacy uniforms against the Arizona Cardinals. New York wore these threads from 1980 to 1999. It was reintroduced in 2022, when the team brought back the navy helmet. Other design elements include classic numbers plus the red-and-blue trim on the jerseys and pants, similar to the uniforms of the 1980s and '90s. Written inside the collar is "Once a Giants, Always a Giant," the words of late owner Wellington Mara. 

The Carolina Panthers, meanwhile, will bring an all-black look to "Sunday Night Football" against the Detroit Lions. Carolina first debuted this all-black combination in 2022. 

The Dallas Cowboys are rocking navy blue alternates with silver pants against the Houston Texans, a look the team will wear only a handful of times each season. The Texans will wear liberty white jerseys with deep steel blue pants. It marks the same uniform matchup the Texans and Cowboys wore for Houston's first regular-season game as a franchise in 2002.

articles.headline: Jalen Hurts challenges underdog Eagles to find out who they are ahead of matchup with Rams
articles.description: — Jalen Hurts isn't used to losing much with the Philadelphia Eagles — only 16 times since 2022 — and he certainly isn't used to getting embarrassed.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Jalen Hurts isn't used to losing much with the Philadelphia Eagles — only 16 times since 2022 — and he certainly isn't used to getting embarrassed.


              Yet from Hurts on down, the Eagles know that's exactly what happened in Chicago in a loss that essentially sent them into an existential crisis only three games into the season. Hurts said he left Chicago following a 27-7 loss with one question for an Eagles team that has not played to championship standards over its first three games.


              “Who are we?” Hurts said.


              Hurts was sacked twice and threw an interception against the Bears. The Eagles were limited to 62 yards of offense in the second half and 248 for the game. He also absorbed a late hit from linebacker D’Marco Jackson along the sideline.


              Hurts' performance was off. He knows the season is in his hands and it's up to him to help the Eagles straighten it out against the Los Angeles Rams.


              “I don’t really care how we look,” Hurts said. “I don’t care who we are. I want to be winners. I want to win, and that’s always going to take precedence over anything.”


              Hurts challenged the Eagles with a question of identity. 


              The battered Rams are in a bigger hole than the Eagles and yet they are modest road favorites in Philadelphia.


              Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson and tight end Terrance Ferguson likely to be sidelined. The Rams should receive a boost by the return of No. 1 wide receiver Puka Nacua after he missed the last two games because of a hip and groin injury.


              “It adds a great football player that’s a huge part of our offense,” coach Sean McVay said, “and it’s a big deal.”


              The connection between quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide receiver Davante Adams flourished for the second straight game without Nacua. Adams caught seven passes for 137 yards despite being covered by arguably the NFL’s cornerback in Patrick Surtain II.


              Can he keep up the stellar production if Nacua returns to the lineup?


              “Well, it doesn’t mean that it’s not going to happen again,” Adams said. “We never know exactly how the plays are going to get called or if he plays or if he doesn’t play.”


              Need to know
              Los Angeles Rams (1-2) at Philadelphia (2-1).

              Latest odds: Rams by 3.


              Against the spread: Rams 1-2; Eagles 0-3.


              Last week: Rams lost to the Broncos 30-26; Eagles lost to the Bears 27-7.


              Last meeting: Eagles beat the Rams 33-26 on Sept. 21, 2025.


              Series record: Eagles lead 26-20-1.

articles.body:
Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City have been alerted to the potential availability of Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, while Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah is on the radar of Real Madrid ahead of next summer. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea, Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Manchester City have been alerted to the potential availability of Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea are actively monitoring the France international, with Xabi Alonso keen on reinforcing his options at right back and the Spanish club looking to raise money to fund their new signings.

- Real Madrid are tracking Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah ahead of next summer, according to Bild. Los Blancos have scouted the 23-year-old England international as they look to add at least two defensive additions to their squad, following his solid displays in Germany since moving from Liverpool for €35 million in 2025, while previous suitors Arsenal are also monitoring developments.

- Tottenham Hotspur have added Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis to their shortlist of future goalkeeping targets alongside Brighton's Bart Verbruggen, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Greece international has impressed so far, with three clean sheets in five Premier League appearances following his £20 million summer move from Olympiakos.

- Bournemouth will not entertain January offers to sign England midfielder Alex Scott despite interest from Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea, reports BBC Sport. The Cherries intend to hold on to the 23-year-old until at least next summer as he enters the final two years of his contract, with transfer valuation of at least £100 million in their minds.

- Real Madrid striker Endrick could face another loan move in January due to a lack of playing time, according to Diario AS. AS Roma maintain an interest in the Brazilian youngster following his previous spell at Lyon, though upcoming opportunities under new Madrid boss José Mourinho could impact his decision.

articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 1

Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs

San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

"I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto

Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season.

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent.
